comments.text: Most people still believe above-ground tombs are strictly due to the wet soil, but the video clearly explains the Spanish and French cultural roots. However, the most fascinating point is that Jazz was born out of burial benevolent societies. Could structural inequality and the lack of insurance for Black communities back then have inadvertently birthed America's greatest musical genre? What are your thoughts on this link between grief and music?

comments.author: @leechumbley5440
comments.text: Thank you for this most informative insight into Louisiana and water. The scale of land lost to water is impressive and will surely continue. In 2005 when Hurricane Katrina struck, 80% of New Orleans was under water. In some tourist broschures River Road is all about Antebellum nostalgia. It was sobering to learn of the slave revolt, a slower form of attrition like cannon fodder, going to die but over 5-10 years. Now it's called Cancer Road, but that's not in the tourist pamphlets. The sea will rise. After Katrina there was talk of the Dutch building a Delta Plan like that currently holding back the North Sea from Holland, but George W. Bush felt that the US did not need any foreign help. New Orleans was home to Kid Ory, Louis Armstrong, Jelly Roll Morton and King Oliver. It has given the world jazz, the only truly American music genre. Will the Mississippi one day break through to the Achafallaya? Helpful to know about the imaginary line around Alexandria separating the wet, Catholic, French-derived south from the red clay, pine forest and cotton of the north. Researchers studying the rate of silt deposit in the Gulf of Mexico from the Mississippi have an exact dating marker – Coca Cola introduced aluminium cans in 1960, so all layers containing these non-rusting cans are post 1960! Thank you for the interesting video.
